| [CASE-353](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-353.md) | Judgement–observation loop with five anchors | The run [LEAD-020](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-020.md) asks for, from [QUESTION-121](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-121.md): "A loop that does not lock in, with action held fixed, and a demonstration that removing a given candidate makes it lock in." [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md)'s meaning–authority loop is built as a bounded simulation inside one mind. Authority sets attention and so attenuates readings against it, and it is scored against the dominant interpretation. The world switches every 300 steps, and nothing the loop does changes the world or when inputs arrive. With sensory input alone the loop locks in on every seed. The question's five candidates are added as switches, each with its stated objection built in. The sensory candidate is split into its channel and exogenous capture. With all present the loop follows every switch, and no single removal makes it lock in. In the minimal loops, removing commitment before evidence, processing signals or exogenous capture makes the loop lock in. Removing an evidence channel (the senses, the body, testimony) leaves it blind, unless capture goes with it. Over 19 parameter variants, a loop with evidence avoided lock-in when it had one of those three anchors in 37 to 42 of 44 configurations per variant. The exceptions are stated. A fictional model, by construction; the numbers are of this model. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [CASE-384](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-384.md) | Planner, value learner and demons in mazes | [CASE-187](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-187.md) run at toy scale for [LEAD-160](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-160.md). Twenty 8x8 mazes with loops, deterministic and fully observed; goal family "reach cell g" for all 64 cells. A planner (M) holds a learned transition table and plans by value iteration; a policy (P) is goal-conditioned Q-learning with hindsight relabelling; a distributed predictor (D) is one TD-learned demon per (state, action, goal) predicting discounted visits under random continuation, acting by ascent. All three learn from the same random walk and treat unknown moves as "stay", which matches their goal success exactly at every level (0.52, 0.83, 1.0, full coverage); M and P choose identical actions, D 93 to 98% the same on average. Queries answered by reading a transition table out of each agent are equally accurate for all three at every level; within each agent's per-decision computation, M answers next states and distances, P distances, D occupancies. A two-entry edit blocking a passage repairs all of M's failed routes, P's 9% and D's 14%; the same block propagated through every demon by the Woodbury identity repairs all of D's, without a table. After a change or damage M recovers fastest and its prediction error flags exactly the damaged units, where P's and D's TD errors flag 56 to 87% of undamaged ones too; 10% damage first costs M more (success 0.27 against 0.35). The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
